technicalSources.title: Indian Standard IS 2470 Part 1 (1985) - design/criteria/construction
technicalSources.finding: Normal septic location open to sky, as far away from exterior building wall as possible, accessible for cleaning.

technicalSources.title: Indian Standard IS 2470 Part 2 (1985) - effluent disposal
technicalSources.finding: Subsurface absorption field at least 6 m from nearest habitable building; 18 m from drinking water source; ground bearing must be protected from effluent.

technicalSources.title: Nepal NBC 208 - sanitary and plumbing design requirements
technicalSources.clause: Sanitary drainage, water tank contamination controls
technicalSources.finding: NBC sanitary/plumbing requirements apply; exact underbuilding tank permission has not been admitted.

technicalSources.title: Pokhara building and infrastructure standards third amendment 2083
technicalSources.finding: Latest amendment publicly listed; its precise effect on underbuilding septic, soak pit, access and setback provisions remains unverified.

components.name: Watertight septic under load-isolated structure / floor
requiredDesignEvidence: Responsible engineer must establish foundation/grade-beam and excavation exclusion zones, relative founding elevations, groundwater uplift, soil stability and waterproofing
Tank is fully sealed and has engineered slab/foundation load path isolated from its walls and cover as applicable
Accessible independent external desludging path and chamber manholes; no access that requires entering living rooms
Safe vent termination above roof/openings with local code verification and inspection access
Sanitary grade, gravity invert, cleanouts, maintenance and odor/gas sealing
Municipal written acceptance of an exception or engineered alternative to normal open-to-sky positioning

components.name: Soak/infiltration pit beneath supporting foundation soils
rationale: Infiltrating effluent into soil supporting foundations introduces settlement, contamination, groundwater and maintenance risks.
Near a habitable building the quoted guidance has a 6m minimum, so a pit underneath it cannot satisfy this technical reference.
Do not call a sealed wastewater tank a 'soak pit'; an impermeable tank has no soil infiltration and needs a separately approved effluent destination.
alternativePath: Investigate sewer availability and authority permission
Assess a non-infiltrating engineered treatment/holding system with lawful discharge/regular removal if approved
Investigate external soil absorption only once survey, actual municipal standards and percolation are available

components.name: Relocate separate exterior WC as an integrated internal washroom
requiredDesignEvidence: Usable clear size, door swing, privacy, plumbing and accessible exit
Structure, slab and sanitary vent coordination
Proof existing common wet-core can serve demand or review actual new interior footprint
Retain exterior WC until new owner-approved revision

components.name: Keep sealed vessel but relocate absorption/disposal separately
requiredDesignEvidence: Public sewer, municipal approved treatment/export, or off-building infiltration route
Percolation/seasonal groundwater and drinking-water source separation
Hydraulic invert/slope or engineered pumping if needed

requiredNextDocuments: Signed surveyed plot boundary, ROW and flood/water-table evidence
Approved footing/foundation plan, plinth/grade beams, bearing areas, access and excavation profiles
Local 2083 amended Pokhara clauses concerning under-building tanks / outfalls
Percolation test and groundwater/well assessment of any actual soil-absorption site
Real septic chamber sizes, baffle/access, invert, vent, watertight slab and deslugging plan
Client/architect decision on separate outside WC versus integration
doNotChange: v3.6 house dimensions and grid cascade
Original DWG/DXF PDFs and source snapshots
Published municipal no-go on options A/B
decision: Study D1, D3 and D4 with real original engineering evidence; do not adopt D2 as ordinary soak pit under the habitable structure. No exact underground location can be chosen without footings and municipal approval.
